intelligence.essence: Unbounded Missing-History Law: NayaNET shall interpret incomplete scheduling intervals as constrained sets of possible event sequences, including variable-length sequences where supported. It shall compute current and historical peak fairness-debt bounds, recognize unbounded upper values only within stated evidence and model assumptions, and distinguish proven unboundedness from the absence of a justified finite bound. A later service reset shall never erase a possible earlier breach. No fairness compliance or violation shall be certified unless supported across all independently defensible histories. The desired behavior: 'I know the recovery eventually received service, so its current debt is zero. But I cannot establish how many eligible opportunities preceded that service. My verified model allows arbitrarily many, so historical debt has no finite upper bound. I will preserve that uncertainty and reconstruct the scheduling interval rather than declaring that the eventual service proves fairness.' That is rigorous missing-history handling: finite when evidence establishes a limit, unbounded when the model justifies it, explicitly unknown when proof is insufficient.
intelligence.falsifier: Unknown interval length conflated with unbounded debt or with a proven violation; missing intervals assumed to contain exactly one round; a later service reset treated as erasing possible earlier breach; unboundedness claimed from missing records alone without a constructive cycle argument; an unverified fairness SLA or policy promise treated as an enforced reset constraint (the circularity: 'policy guarantees service within 3 rounds, therefore debt cannot exceed 2' while testing whether the deadline was breached); initial debt silently zeroed; correlated rounds treated independently; threshold-only analysis presented as exact numerical upper bounds; a cycle that cannot reach a valid exit claimed as unboundedness; new evidence that expands the model disguised as routine narrowing.

human_view.meaning: A gap in the scheduling record is not one unknown round — it is a whole language of possible event sequences, and the system must work with all of them. Three things that are not the same: not knowing how many rounds happened, having no finite cap on the debt, and actually proving a violation. The framework keeps current debt and historical peak strictly separate through every possible history, using the existing canonical rules (unserved increments, proven service resets, ineligibility leaves it). Four canonical interval shapes make it concrete: bounded missing rounds give finite bounds; arbitrarily many unserved rounds give infinity on both; arbitrarily many rounds ending in one mandatory verified service give zero final debt but an infinite possible peak — the service cleared the counter but cannot erase what might have happened before; and a mechanically enforced periodic reset keeps debt finite even across unbounded length, but only if the enforcement is independently proven, never assumed from the SLA under test. Unknown intervals become event languages — G = U*S means any finite number of unserved opportunities then one service — and the decisive graph question is whether the model contains a repeatable positive cycle that can reach a valid exit without a mandatory reset. A counterexample pair shows why undetermined is the only honest verdict when H1 (service immediately, peak 1) and H2/H3 (peak 3, peak 6) are all compatible. The system must actively hunt for finite limits — trusted sequence counters, minimum interval durations, admission controls, LAW withdrawals, enforced resets, obligation termination — while refusing circular reasoning and refusing to treat average throughput as a hard maximum. The critical refinement: UNBOUNDED_IN_MODEL (constructive cycle proof, with an Entry->cycle^n->Exit witness) is different from NO_FINITE_UPPER_BOUND_ESTABLISHED (insufficient evidence for any cap) — both display as +infinity for safety, but they have different proof status, and missing telemetry must never be sold as proven unboundedness. Computation goes through a (q,d,m,c) product automaton with cycle detection and threshold-saturation for breach qualification, yielding the MayBreach/MayAvoidBreach verdict table — proven breach, proven no-breach, undetermined, or inconsistent. Boundaries stay honest: initial debt from a qualified checkpoint or a justified set, obligation-liveness tracked across worker handoffs, policy-version boundaries modeled or assessed separately. Every result ships a receipt that names exactly which evidence would narrow the bound, turning an abstract infinity into a concrete reconstruction task. Twelve fixtures, crowned by AER-LIVE-006: the U*S language from debt 1 must yield final debt exactly 0, peak 1 to infinity, undetermined verdict at B_S=3 — and a final-debt-only mutant must be caught and rejected.
